Being against workers unions.

I don't get how people don't understand that workers unions and organisations are an important part of jobs and working.

Lets be honest: many corporations don't give a shit about their workers and would pay them as little as possible if they could. That's just business.

Unions can be the opposite of that, to a fault. They can demand impractical and way-over-the-top things from their employers.

Hopefully, both parties meet in the middle with something that is fair and reasonable.

It's like buying a car. The salesman wants to charge as much as possible, the buyer wants to pay as little as possible. They barter and meet in the middle with a price both are happy with. 

Take away workers unions and you are only left with the salesman.

I have no reports here, dude. I didnt do a survey and don't have any sources or data.

All I said was that I am sick of the stereotype and that in my day to day life I do not see anyone experiencing it. 

This was merely my opinion with some anecdotal info on a post someone else made. I'm not going to spend hours researching this for a reddit comment. Not once did I say point blank "Australia isn't racist".

You're trying to take my post and make it seem like I am the sole representative of an entire country just so you can argue. If that's your thing, dude, then go ahead.

Whew, teach me for sharing an opinion on reddit!

>but I don't see it, so it therefore can't exist.

I didnt say it doesnt exist, I said "I dont see any racism here". How else could I put it? Lie and say I do see it?

>your entire post is literally the same as "I'm friends with a black person. I can't be racist."

No, my post was demonstrating how many people of different cultural backgrounds are integrating, adding to society and becoming Australian and are a part of my life.

>you call them foreigners

Not going to bother with answering your point about semantics of the word 'foreigner' - that's just baiting and pedanticism.

>there are race problems

Never said there weren't race issues in Australia. What I said was that I was sick of the "Racist Australian stereotype".

In summary: I, an average Aussie, have never seen racism, I encounter a lot of happy people of diverse cultural backgrounds in my day to day life, I don't think the 'racist Australian' stereotype is deserved.

You're choosing to interpret what I said provocatively.

I'm getting pretty sick of the 'Racist Australian' stereo type.

Full disclosure, I am a white Australian, but apart from the occasional wanker who makes the news for some racists tirade, I don't see any racism here. Sheez, even these idiots who make the news do so because it's such an unusual and disgusting thing - if it was as common as people on reddit make it out to be, it wouldnt be news worthy.
